title: Capacity Intent Editor: Scaling Scenarios & Change Archive
creator: Claire Nguyen
description:
Summary: Build a Capacity Intent Editor inside the Console that lets operators compose, preview, and archive scaling intents for Dedicated fleets. This UI surfaces: 1) scaling controls (min/max/target, burst windows, cooldowns), 2) throughput guarantees and backed SLAs per intent, 3) scenario simulator to estimate observed throughput & cost under traffic traces, and 4) an immutable change archive with diffs and rollback links.

Why this exists: customers running Dedicated capacity ask for a single place to declare desired capacity intent (instead of ad-hoc instance edits). The editor formalizes intent as first-class objects that the autoscaler and operator tooling can act on. It needs to be auditable and paired with throughput projections so SREs and customer admins can reason about risk/cost tradeoffs before rollout.

Scope & goals: Deliver a console-first editor that ties to the Dedicated control-plane APIs (ENG contracts exist), supports canarying intents to a subset of pools, and stores an append-only change history with operator annotations. The scenario simulator will run client-side projections using sampled recent traffic (from Console telemetry API) and run in O(200ms) for small traces; if heavy, it will drop to background job and link to a job result.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement server-side autoscaler changes (already owned by ENG-28412) or billing quota enforcement. It does not aim to add RBAC beyond existing role checks—this will be a follow-up.

Design/PRD links:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Capacity+Intent+Editor+PRD
- Design spec (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/capacity-intent-editor
- API contract (internal doc): https://go.redwood.ai/dedicated-intent-api

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Operators can create, edit, preview, and archive an intent object from Console.
- Preview simulation produces throughput/cost delta estimates given last-24h traffic trace and highlights SLO risk bands.
- Change archive records who made the change, timestamp, fields changed, and a one-click rollback that opens a revert intent PR.
- Intent creation triggers a phantom canary mode that can be limited to a single pool for 1–24h.
- UI surfaces clear guidance and warnings for potential customer-impacting configurations (e.g., underprovisioning poll frequency < 30s).

Engineering notes (contract & telemetry):
- Contract version: Dedicated Intent API v1.2 (ENG-30899 for schema updates). We expect endpoints: POST /intents, PATCH /intents/{id}, GET /intents/{id}/simulation. Simulation may be served synchronously for sample sizes < 2k tokens, otherwise returns job id.
- Telemetry: use console-telemetry v2 tags: intent_id, pool_id, simulation_sample_n, sim_estimated_cost_microcents.
- Rollout: feature-flag gated (ff: capacity_intent_editor) to 25% internal accounts, then staged to all accounts after 2 weeks and Obs validation.

Operational playbook (short):
- If simulations are failing (>=5% of attempts), the UI shows degraded state and suggests opening ENG-30899 with sample ids.
- For revert flow: creating a rollback intent generates an audit log entry and triggers a canary to verify before global application.

Open trade-offs discussed:
- Store full diff vs. snapshot: we opted for per-change snapshot to simplify rollback and retain cheap reads. Snapshots increase storage but simplify reconciliation logic with autoscaler.
- Simulation placement: client-side gives immediate feedback but risks leaking sampled traffic; decided to run client-side with sampled anonymization and an opt-out toggle. Full traces run as background jobs.

Out-of-scope follow-ups:
- RBAC matrix for per-intent approvals (future ticket).
- Billing-aware recommendations in simulation (future integration with Billing team).

QA checklist:
- Create/edit/rollback flows tested across three pool types (small/medium/large).
- Simulation results verified against server-side simulation service for consistency within 5%.
- Audit log entries present in Console's change history and match timestamps from the control plane.

Rollout plan:
- Canary to Redwood internal orgs (2026-03-01), gather ops feedback.
- Expand to customers with test flags (2026-03-15).
- Full release in console-2026.03 after 2 weeks of telemetry validation.

Notes: See linked GitHub PRs and temporary design sketches in Drive. Reach out to Claire/Diego for walkthroughs.
acceptance_criteria: Create, edit, preview, and archive intent objects in Console
Simulation produces throughput and cost delta estimates using last-24h traffic samples
Immutable change archive with author, timestamp, field diffs, and rollback link
Canary mode limited to single pool for 1-24h
